title: Greek lemon chicken with potatoes
description: Chicken legs roasted on potatoes with lots of lemon, garlic and oregano, until the skin is crisp and the potatoes soft and golden.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Peel the potatoes and cut them into long wedges. Crush the garlic.

steps.text: In a large roasting tin mix most of the olive oil, the juice of both lemons, the garlic, oregano, salt and pepper. Add the potatoes and chicken and turn everything to coat.
steps.tip: Lots of lemon is the point: the potatoes soak it up and turn soft inside and golden outside.

steps.text: Turn the chicken skin side up on top of the potatoes. Crumble the stock cube into {250 ml} hot water and pour it into the tin around the chicken.
steps.tip: The liquid steams the potatoes first, then cooks away so they brown.

steps.text: Roast for 1 hour, turning the potatoes once halfway, until the chicken skin is crisp and the potatoes are golden.
steps.tip: Add a splash of water if the tin dries out before the potatoes are soft. The chicken is done when the juices near the bone run clear.

steps: Meanwhile chop the tomatoes and cucumber into a simple salad with a pinch of salt and the last of the oil.

steps.text: Serve the chicken and potatoes with the pan juices spooned over, and the salad.
steps.tip: Leftovers keep 3 days and make a good cold lunch.

title: Spanakopita (spinach and feta pie)
description: Crisp layers of filo around spinach, feta, fresh cheese and dill. A Greek pie that is just as good cold the next day.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 190 °C. Thaw frozen spinach, or wilt fresh spinach in a big pot and let it cool. Squeeze it very dry with your hands, a handful at a time.
steps.tip: Squeeze hard: wet spinach makes a soggy pie.

steps: Chop the onion finely and soften it in {1 tbsp} of the olive oil for 5 minutes.

steps.text: In a bowl mix the spinach, onion, crumbled feta, cottage cheese, eggs, dill, nutmeg and pepper.
steps.tip: No salt needed: the feta is salty.

steps.text: Brush a baking tin of about 25 x 35 cm with oil. Lay in half the filo sheets, brushing each one lightly with oil.
steps.tip: Keep the filo under a damp towel while you work, it dries out fast.

steps: Spread the filling evenly, then cover with the rest of the filo, brushing each sheet. Tuck in the edges and brush the top.

steps.text: Score the top into squares with a sharp knife and bake for 40 to 45 minutes until deep golden and crisp.
steps.tip: Scoring first means the crisp top does not shatter when you cut it.

steps.text: Let it rest for 10 minutes before cutting. It is good warm or cold.
steps.tip: It keeps 3 days in the fridge. Warm pieces in the oven to crisp them up.

title: Greek baked fish with tomatoes (plaki)
description: White fish baked under a thick sauce of tomatoes, onions, peppers and parsley. Bring bread to wipe the dish.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C. Slice the onions and pepper thinly and chop the garlic and parsley.
Heat the olive oil in a pan on medium and soften the onions and pepper for 10 minutes. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, oregano, half the parsley and half the salt and simmer for 10 minutes until thick.

steps.text: Season the fish with the rest of the salt and the juice of half the lemon. Spread half the sauce in a baking dish, lay the fish on it and cover it with the rest.
steps.tip: Using frozen hake? Thaw it in the fridge overnight and pat it dry.

steps.text: Bake uncovered for 20 minutes, until the fish is white all the way through and flakes easily.
steps.tip: Check the thickest piece with a fork.

steps.text: Scatter with the rest of the parsley and serve with bread and lemon wedges.
steps.tip: The sauce is the best part, so do not skip the bread.

title: Pumpkin risotto
description: Creamy autumn risotto where the pumpkin melts into the rice and turns it orange, finished with parmesan and toasted pumpkin seeds.

steps.text: Peel the pumpkin, scoop out the seeds and cut it into small 1 cm cubes. Chop the onion and garlic. Crumble the stock cubes into {1200 ml} hot water and keep it warm on low heat.
steps.tip: Hot stock keeps the rice cooking evenly.

steps: Heat the olive oil in a wide pan on medium heat and soften the onion for 5 minutes. Add the pumpkin and garlic and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes until the grains look a little see-through at the edges.
Pour in the wine and stir until it has almost all bubbled away.

steps.text: Add a ladle of hot stock and stir until it is almost absorbed, then add the next. Keep going for 18 minutes, stirring often.
steps.tip: The pumpkin melts into the rice and makes it creamy. Taste a grain: soft with a tiny bite in the middle.

steps.text: Meanwhile toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan for 3 minutes until they start to pop.
steps.tip: Shake the pan and take them out straight away, or they burn.

steps.text: Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the butter, grated parmesan and a pinch of nutmeg, cover and leave for 2 minutes. Serve topped with the seeds.
steps.tip: Risotto should flow slowly on the plate. Add a splash of stock if it is too stiff.

title: Pasta alla Norma
description: Sicilian pasta with golden fried eggplant in a garlicky tomato sauce, topped with ricotta and parmesan.

steps.text: Cut the eggplants into 2 cm cubes, toss them with {1 tsp} of the salt and leave them in a colander for 15 minutes.
steps.tip: Salting draws out water, so the eggplant fries golden and soaks up less oil.

steps: Pat the eggplant dry. Heat {4 tbsp} of the olive oil in a large pan on medium-high and fry it for 10 minutes, turning, until golden and soft. Lift it out.
Add the rest of the oil, the sliced garlic and the chili to the pan for 1 minute, then the tomatoes, basil and the rest of the salt. Simmer for 15 minutes until thick.

steps.text: Meanwhile cook the pasta in salted water until al dente.
steps.tip: Keep a mug of the pasta water before you drain it.

steps: Stir the eggplant into the sauce, then toss it with the drained pasta and a splash of the pasta water.

steps.text: Serve with spoonfuls of ricotta on top and grated parmesan.
steps.tip: In Sicily they use salted ricotta. A little extra parmesan gives the same salty bite.

title: Egg curry with rice
description: Boiled eggs simmered in a spiced onion, tomato and coconut sauce with spinach. A cheap, filling Indian home curry.

steps.text: Start the rice: rinse it, put it in a pot with {550 ml} water and a pinch of salt, bring to the boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat.
steps.tip: Keeping the lid on is what makes rice fluffy. Do not peek while it cooks.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool them in cold water and peel them.
steps.tip: Eggs that are a week or two old peel more easily than very fresh ones.

steps: Chop the onions finely and grate the garlic and ginger. Heat the oil in a pan on medium and fry the onions for 10 minutes until golden.

steps.text: Add the garlic, ginger, curry powder, turmeric and cumin and stir for 1 minute.
steps.tip: Keep stirring so the spices do not burn. Add a spoon of water if the pan is dry.

steps: Add the tomatoes, coconut milk, salt and {100 ml} water and simmer for 10 minutes until thick.

steps.text: Make a few shallow cuts in each egg. Add them to the sauce with the spinach and simmer for 5 minutes, spooning the sauce over.
steps.tip: The cuts let the sauce soak into the eggs.

steps: Serve with the rice, two eggs each.

title: Aloo gobi with chickpeas
description: Potatoes and cauliflower cooked in turmeric and cumin until tender, with chickpeas for protein. A gentle, everyday Indian dish.
steps: Cut the cauliflower into small florets and the potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Chop the onion and grate the garlic and ginger. Drain the chickpeas.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large pan with a lid on medium heat. Fry the cumin for a few seconds until it sizzles, then the onion for 6 minutes until soft.
steps.tip: Frying whole spices in oil first wakes up their flavour.

steps: Add the garlic, ginger, turmeric and curry powder for 1 minute, then the potatoes and cauliflower. Toss for 3 minutes until coated in the spices.

steps.text: Add the tomatoes, chickpeas, salt and {100 ml} water. Cover and cook on low for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the potato is soft.
steps.tip: Keep the lid on so the vegetables steam. Add a splash of water if it starts to stick.

steps.text: Squeeze over the lemon, taste for salt and serve with warm flatbread.
steps.tip: It keeps 3 days and is good in a lunch box.

title: Oyakodon (chicken and egg rice bowl)
description: Chicken and onion simmered in a sweet soy broth, set with soft egg and spooned over rice. Japanese comfort food in 30 minutes.

steps.text: Start the rice: rinse it, put it in a pot with {550 ml} water and a pinch of salt, bring to the boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat.
steps.tip: Keeping the lid on is what makes rice fluffy. Do not peek while it cooks.

steps: Slice the onions thinly and cut the chicken into bite-size pieces. Crumble the stock cube into {300 ml} hot water and stir in the soy sauce and sugar.
Put the onion and the broth in a frying pan with a lid. Simmer for 5 minutes until the onion is soft.
Add the chicken and simmer for 7 minutes, turning once, until cooked through.

steps.text: Beat the eggs lightly, just a few strokes, and pour them over the chicken. Cover and cook on low for 2 minutes, until just set but still soft on top.
steps.tip: Do not over-beat or over-cook: the egg should be silky and a little runny.

steps.text: Spoon the rice into bowls and slide the chicken and egg on top with some of the broth. Scatter with sliced spring onion.
steps.tip: Oyako means parent and child: the chicken and the egg in one bowl.

title: Chicken tortilla soup
description: A smoky Mexican soup of chicken, black beans, corn and tomato, topped with crushed tortilla chips, cheese and avocado.
steps: Chop the onion, garlic and pepper. Drain and rinse the beans and drain the sweetcorn.
Heat the oil in a large pot on medium and soften the onion and pepper for 6 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin, paprika and chili for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, beans, corn, the crumbled stock cube and {1000 ml} water and bring to a simmer.

steps.text: Add the chicken breasts whole and poach them in the soup for 15 minutes, until cooked through.
steps.tip: Poaching keeps the chicken juicy. Cut the thickest piece to check there is no pink.

steps: Lift out the chicken, shred it with two forks and put it back in the pot. Squeeze in the lemon juice and taste for salt.

steps.text: Serve in bowls topped with crushed tortilla chips, grated cheese and sliced avocado.
steps.tip: Add the chips at the table so they stay crunchy. The soup keeps 3 days.

title: Turkish red lentil soup (mercimek)
description: A smooth, golden soup of red lentils, carrot and potato, finished with paprika oil and a big squeeze of lemon.
steps: Rinse the lentils. Chop the onion, carrot and potato small and chop the garlic.
Heat {2 tbsp} of the olive oil in a pot on medium and soften the onion and carrot for 6 minutes.
Add the garlic, tomato paste and cumin and stir for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, potato, the crumbled stock cube and {1200 ml} water. Simmer for 25 minutes until everything is very soft.

steps.text: Blend until smooth with a stick blender. Add a little water if it is too thick.
steps.tip: It should be smooth and pourable, like thick cream.

steps.text: Warm the rest of the oil with the paprika and chili for a few seconds and drizzle it over the bowls. Serve with lemon wedges and bread.
steps.tip: A good squeeze of lemon in each bowl is what makes it taste Turkish. It keeps 4 days.

title: Cottage pie (beef and potato bake)
description: Beef mince with carrots and peas in a rich gravy, under a thick layer of cheesy mash baked until golden.
steps: Peel the potatoes, cut them into chunks and boil them in salted water for 20 minutes until soft.
Meanwhile chop the onion and dice the carrots. Heat the oil in a large pan on medium and fry the onion and carrot for 6 minutes.

steps.text: Turn the heat up, add the mince and brown it for 8 minutes, breaking it up. Stir in the flour and tomato paste for 1 minute.
steps.tip: Let the meat sit for a minute at a time so it browns rather than steams.

steps.text: Crumble in the stock cube, add {300 ml} water and the pepper and simmer for 15 minutes until thick. Stir in the peas.
steps.tip: It should be juicy but not runny, or the mash sinks into it.

steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Drain the potatoes and mash them with the warm milk, butter and salt.

steps.text: Spread the meat in a baking dish, cover it with the mash and rough up the top with a fork. Scatter with the grated cheese.
steps.tip: The fork ridges turn crisp and golden.

steps.text: Bake for 25 minutes until golden and bubbling at the edges. Let it rest for 5 minutes before serving.
steps.tip: It keeps 3 days and freezes well in portions.

title: Fish fingers with mash and peas
description: Oven-crisp fish fingers with buttery mash and peas. The easy weeknight fish dinner children actually eat.
steps: Peel the potatoes, cut them into chunks and boil them in salted water for 20 minutes until soft.

steps.text: Heat the oven as the fish finger packet says, usually 220 °C, and bake the fish fingers for about 15 minutes, turning once.
steps.tip: The oven makes them crispier than the frying pan, with no extra oil.

steps: Cook the peas in a little boiling water for 3 minutes, then drain.
Drain the potatoes and mash them with the warm milk, butter and salt.

steps.text: Serve the fish fingers with the mash, peas and a lemon wedge.
steps.tip: For mushy peas, crush the peas with a fork and a little butter.

title: Sausage and bean casserole
description: Browned sausages simmered with beans, peppers and smoky paprika in tomato sauce. One pan, very little work.
steps: Slice the onion and pepper and chop the garlic. Drain and rinse the beans.
Heat the oil in a wide pan with a lid on medium-high and brown the sausages for 6 minutes, turning. Lift them out and cut each one in half.
Soften the onion and pepper in the same pan for 6 minutes, then add the garlic, paprika and tomato paste for 1 minute.

steps.text: Add the tomatoes, beans, sausages and {150 ml} water. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick.
steps.tip: Crush a few beans against the side of the pan to thicken the sauce.

steps.text: Taste for salt and serve with bread.
steps.tip: It keeps 3 days and freezes well.

title: Chinese tomato and egg stir-fry
description: Soft scrambled eggs folded into a sweet and savoury tomato sauce over rice. One of China's best-loved home dishes, ready in 25 minutes.

steps.text: Start the rice: rinse it, put it in a pot with {550 ml} water and a pinch of salt, bring to the boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat.
steps.tip: Keeping the lid on is what makes rice fluffy. Do not peek while it cooks.

steps: Cut the tomatoes into wedges, chop the garlic and slice the spring onion. Beat the eggs with half the salt.

steps.text: Heat {2 tbsp} of the oil in a wok or frying pan on high. Pour in the eggs and stir gently until just set in large soft curds, about 1 minute. Tip them onto a plate.
steps.tip: Take them out while still a little wet: they go back in at the end.

steps: Add the rest of the oil and the garlic for a few seconds, then the tomatoes. Stir-fry for 3 minutes until they soften and release their juice.

steps.text: Add the sugar, soy sauce, the rest of the salt and {50 ml} water and let it bubble for 2 minutes into a light sauce.
steps.tip: The sugar balances the sourness of the tomatoes. That is how it is made in Chinese homes.

steps: Put the eggs back, fold them in gently, add the spring onion and serve over the rice.
